narrative.summary: This 70,977 sq ft parcel at 414 Grant St is currently occupied by county government and mapped to the GT-B zoning district. The encoded rule set does not yet support GT-B, so use-table compatibility for Two-Unit Residential cannot be determined from this screening. No barriers were identified in the currently evaluated mapped hazard layers (steep slope, landslide, mine, flood).
key_bottlenecks: GT-B district is not encoded in the preliminary use-table logic, preventing automated determination of whether Two-Unit Residential is permitted, conditional, or prohibited. This is the sole material constraint requiring resolution before any entitlement pathway can be identified.
narrative.why_this_matters: No barriers were identified in the currently evaluated mapped hazard layers. The screening cannot confirm or rule out zoning compatibility because the GT-B district is not yet supported by the encoded rule set. Official interpretation from Pittsburgh zoning staff or the Zoning Administrator is required to determine whether Two-Unit Residential is a permitted, conditional, or prohibited use in GT-B. Until that interpretation is obtained, no entitlement pathway can be identified.
what_could_change_the_result: Official zoning interpretation confirming the use-table status of Two-Unit Residential in the GT-B district, which would establish whether the proposed housing type is permitted by right, requires conditional approval, or is prohibited.
questions_for_human_review: What is the use-table status of Two-Unit Residential in the GT-B (Golden Triangle – Business) zoning district under Pittsburgh Zoning Code § 911.02?
Does the current county government occupancy create any additional entitlement or procedural considerations for converting the parcel to residential use, beyond standard zoning use-table compliance?
narrative.limitations: All currently implemented core hazard layers (steep slope, landslide, mine, flood) were evaluated for this parcel, but this does not constitute a complete site-design, infrastructure, environmental, or regulatory assessment. The GT-B zoning district is not yet encoded in the preliminary use-table logic, so zoning compatibility cannot be determined without official interpretation.
